approach: Use the released repo exactly as a full_release: clone/install the pinned requirements, then extract only the notebook's Code-section cells into an importable module and the single-run synthetic experimental cell for C1. The wrapper sets the documented seeds, executes the authors' C1 cell/classes unchanged, and does not run the multi-run, jazz, polbooks, or polblogs experiments. It then computes the C1 sum-absolute estimation error from the final SubSearch subgraph using the authors' spectral-clustering and plug-in estimator, records C2-C4 cheap baselines, and writes results/metrics.json. A tiny --smoke mode proves the same data flow before the full 1000-step S.A. run.

files.purpose: Load robust_estim_sbm.ipynb as JSON, track the markdown headings for the Code and Experiments sections, extract all Code-section code cells into src/authors_code.py, and extract only the C1 single-run synthetic experiment cell into src/c1_experiment_cell.py; do not execute the notebook or rewrite author logic.

Generated unchanged from the notebook Code section by extract_authors_notebook.py; contains the author implementations of SBM generation/corruption, spectral clustering, Qhat(S), cost c(S), SubSearch S.A., and baselines.

Thin helper module that imports src/authors_code.py, computes sum_{k,l}|Gamma_kl - Gamma_hat_kl| over all K^2 entries, oracle and pruning baselines, outlier count in S_best, and writes metric dictionaries; no replacement of author estimator code.

Single entrypoint. Ensures the repo exists, invokes extraction if needed, sets seeds, executes the extracted C1 experiment cell/source in a guarded namespace, collects the final subgraph/estimates, writes results/metrics.json, and supports --smoke and --checks modes.
Final metric output containing C1 value, pass/fail against the 10% relative tolerance, configuration/seeds, runtime, C2-C4 cheap diagnostics, and C7 outlier count if available.

config.install: pip install -r requirements.txt from repo; pins numpy==1.26.0, matplotlib==3.7.1, seaborn==0.13.1, scikit-learn==1.3.2, scipy==1.13.1, tqdm==4.66.5, pandas==2.1.4, scikit-network unpinned, jupyter (repo requirements.txt)
config.graph_seed: 12345 (A2; paper does not state graph seed)
config.graph_type: simple undirected, no self-loops; E[A]=Q-diag(Q) with Q=Z Gamma Z^T (R1)
config.corruption: exactly m nodes; for outlier i and community k draw Beta(alpha=p*eps, beta=(1-p)*eps) with p=Gamma_{z(i),k}, eps=1e-3, sample Bernoulli edges and overwrite incident edges (R2/A3)
config.initial_subgraph: BFS growth from uniformly random seed, adding uniformly random boundary nodes until size 140 (A4/R6)
config.proposal: uniform random boundary edge (u in S, v outside adjacent to S), swap u and v (A5/R7)
config.clustering: symmetric normalized Laplacian spectral clustering with known K; KMeans k-means++ n_init=10 random_state=0 (R5/A6)
config.Gamma_hat_plugin: empirical edge density per S_k x S_l: (1/(|S_k||S_l|)) sum_{i in S_k,j in S_l} A_ij (R3)
config.final_labels: spectral clustering on S_best, then plug-in density estimate (A10)
config.T0: 2.25 (paper C1 config), using author experimental cell; adaptive rule R11: chain 100, accept rate >=0.90, multiply by 1.5, cap 50 doublings, only if cell does not fix T0 (A8)
config.stopping: range max-min of S_best cost over last 25 chains < 1e-4 (A9/R10)
config.error_sum: sum over all K^2 entries |Gamma_kl - Gamma_hat_kl| including symmetric duplicates (A11)
config.pruning_baseline: num_to_prune=gamma*n=60; remove 60/K=30 highest- and 30 lowest-degree nodes per community plus resulting isolated nodes, then recluster (R13)
config.filtering_baseline: Acharya et al. filtering: start S0=G, iteratively remove a node sampled proportionally to squared entries of the top eigenvector of A_S-Qhat(S), up to n/2 removals (R15)
config.oracle: subgraph of true inlier nodes with true community labels (C2)
config.jazz_optional: if executed, unweighted simple undirected jazz graph n=198, |S|=178, K=3, n_iters_inner=19, SA seed=12345, cooling 0.99, t_max=1000, t_tol=25, epsilon=1e-4 (C5/A13/A14); not part of C1 run

smoke.purpose: fast data-flow check only, not compared to C1

config.runtime_expected: ~14 min for C1 S.A. on paper hardware; baselines <5 s

steps: Clone https://github.com/leobianco/robust_estim_sbm/ if absent and install requirements with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`; if scikit-network resolution fails, install a current scikit-network release explicitly.

Run `python extract_authors_notebook.py --notebook robust_estim_sbm.ipynb`; it must write src/authors_code.py and src/c1_experiment_cell.py, extracting only Code-section cells plus the C1 experiment cell matching n=200, K=2, gamma=0.3, t_max=1000.

Import-test src/authors_code.py with `python -c 'import src.authors_code'`; inspect src/c1_experiment_cell.py to confirm the experiment cell instantiates the C1 config and calls the author run() method, and record the result variable names used by reproduce.py.
Run the smoke test `python reproduce.py --smoke` and verify results/metrics_smoke.json contains finite cost and finite estimation error with the tiny config.

Run `python reproduce.py --checks` or equivalent: generate the n=200 C1 graph with graph_seed=12345, assert 60 outlier flags/140 inliers, check symmetry/no self-loops, build a connected |S|=140 initial subgraph, run one spectral clustering/Qhat/cost evaluation, and compute C2-C4 baselines.
Run the full C1 experiment with `python reproduce.py`; reproduce.py seeds numpy/python with 12345, executes the extracted author C1 cell unchanged, and times the run.

After S.A., recover S_best from the author result object or namespace, run the author spectral clustering/plug-in estimator on S_best, and compute sum_{k,l in {1..K}} |Gamma_kl - Gamma_hat_kl| over all K^2 entries.
Compute C7 outlier count as the number of true corrupted nodes included in S_best; optionally compute C2 oracle and C3/C4 pruning diagnostics using author baseline code.
Compare C1 to 0.05 with a 10% relative tolerance (accept 0.045-0.055), write results/metrics.json with value, pass boolean, seeds, config, runtime, outlier count, and baseline diagnostics.

If the full run exceeds about 12-14 CPU minutes before t_max=1000, use the documented scale-down only as a last resort: t_max=600-700 or cooling 0.99 with early stopping already active; record the shorter configuration and mark C1 partial if the value drifts outside tolerance.
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` generates a tiny n=40, K=2, gamma=0.3 SBM, corrupts m=12 nodes, picks a connected |S|=28 subgraph, runs 3 S.A. outer steps with L_t=5, computes the spectral cost and sum-absolute error, and writes results/metrics_smoke.json. Success means the extracted author functions, graph generation, corruption, clustering, cost, and metric writer all execute end-to-end in seconds.
intermediate_checks: Notebook extraction: confirm src/authors_code.py is non-empty, imports cleanly, and contains the author SBM generation, corruption, spectral clustering, Qhat/cost, SubSearch, pruning, and filtering definitions; confirm only the C1 experiment cell was extracted from the Experiments section.

Generated graph: n=200, K=2, exactly m=60 nodes marked outliers, 140 inliers, adjacency symmetric, diagonal zero, edge count in a plausible SBM range for Gamma diag 0.65/off-diagonal 0.35 after corruption.
Initial subgraph: |S|=140, connected, and contains a mix of inlier/outlier nodes; spectral clustering with K=2 returns two non-empty clusters; Qhat(S) is 140x140 and c(S) is finite.

Baseline sanity on the fixed graph seed: oracle sum-absolute error near 0.02, pruning sum-absolute error near 0.353, pruning cost near 22.15, and pruning keeps about 27/60 outliers; large deviations indicate a graph-seed/corruption mismatch.
Runtime pilot: time 5-10 S.A. steps and extrapolate; if projected C1 exceeds ~15 min on this CPU, reduce t_max only after recording the deviation, because the paper value assumes t_max=1000.
Parameter check: K^2=4 connectivity parameters are estimated; compute the error over all 4 entries, not only the upper triangle.
Final result check: S_best should contain roughly 5 of the 60 outliers; C1 error should be near 0.05 within 0.045-0.055.
budget_plan: About 20-24 min total: 0-5 min clone and pip install pinned requirements; 5-7 min notebook extraction and import checks; 7-8 min smoke test; 8-10 min C1 graph/baseline checks and runtime pilot; 10-23 min full C1 S.A. with t_max=1000 and L_t=60; 23-24 min final metric computation and JSON write. C2-C4 baselines cost seconds. If setup or S.A. overruns, preserve the 10% tolerance check and record actual runtime/value; only shorten t_max/cooling if the full run is projected beyond ~15 min and mark any deviation as partial.
